runs.rationale_summary: The run hit the 50-call limit (LimitsExceeded) without submitting. defects4j failed on the missing Perl module, so the agent re-simulated the chain in Java, got 112.5 against 87.5, and its last experiments built a 'Correct drift: (-50,0)', i.e. it was heading toward blaming drift. It read Plot.nudge in full, never grepped tests for drift, and so never saw testDrift.

The run hit the 50-call limit with no submission. The agent compiled its own TestRunner, saw 0x12345600 against 0xf12345600, and drafted an overlay fix ('m_corrected = field << shift'). It found BitField.setValue's pre-shifted overlay call only in its last two calls (#44-45) and never used it.

On the control, the agent diagnosed NumberUtils.overlay correctly ('shift = (index + at) * width should be index * width + at') and wrote that ranking into /tmp/ranking.txt. It then kept reading sibling converters until it hit the 50-call limit and never called submit. Several calls were also lost to unavailable test runners (defects4j, mvn).

In 8 calls the agent read Plot.resolve in full, including the delta lines past the guard padding, and hand-computed 112.5. Its evidence_chain then states 'The offset direction is reversed in drift', so it assumed the drift sign convention. Its caller grep covered source/ only, so it never retrieved PlotUtilitiesTests.testDrift.

In 7 calls the agent read every hop, compose included, then blamed overlay because 'the mask m = field << (index*width) leaves out at'. It never searched for overlay's other caller, BitField.setValue, which pins the pre-shifted-field contract. It also never ran or simulated the test, and its ranking follows strict depth order (overlay, combine, widen, compose).

The agent hand-computed 112.5 and saw that the sign was inverted somewhere in drift, nudge or shift. It settled the question by reading drift's javadoc as 'a drift from the unexploded point to the exploded point, which means it should be p2-p1', a convention the javadoc never states. Its caller grep covered source/ only, so it never saw testDrift.

A Java re-simulation reproduced 112.5, and showing that p2-p1 fixes it led to 'sign is inverted in PlotUtilities.drift()'. It ruled out shift (maxY-height equals y) and called resolve 'correct; bug is upstream', then ranked ring, rim and getArcBounds above resolve. It never searched tests, so it never saw testDrift. Its test attempts failed (Perl module, ant, javac 1.4).

Its evidence_chain says 'drift should represent the direction from unexploded to exploded (point2 - point1)... The subtraction is backwards', supported by a Java simulation in which the corrected drift passes. It searched tests only for getArcBounds callers; the PlotUtilities/drift grep was limited to source/, so testDrift was never retrieved. It ranked nudge 5th, behind the shallow hops.

Its evidence_chain says 'drift should compute point2-point1 (exploded-unexploded) to get the direction of explosion... primary bug'. It noted nudge 'Could alternatively fix the sign here' but still ranked it 5th, below rim, ring and getArcBounds. It never searched tests for drift, so testDrift was not retrieved. defects4j and ant were unavailable.

It ranked wordOffset first because 'the javadoc states index * width + at, but the implementation uses (index + at) * width', and put apply second as 'same formula inversion'. It had displayed widen, where wordOffset only feeds the 'run does not fit' guard, yet its simulation still wrongly treated wordOffset's 256 as the shift amount. It also probed git log/diff, which the protocol forbids.

This was a provider stall: 19 tool calls finished by 06:22:57 (trajectory timestamps), then the session was silent for about 250 s until the 300 s SIGTERM. The empty exit status matches a hung model request, not slow investigation. The agent had read every hop, compose included, and was still looking for a test runner.

The agent found BitField.setValue and simulated it, concluding 'setValue is NOT directly affected (mask is pre-shifted). The bug only affects cases where at > 0 and field is an unshifted base mask'. That is the pin pointing at compose, yet it still submitted 'mask should be field << (at + index*width)' with overlay first and compose 4th, in depth order.

The agent first drafted an overlay fix, then retrieved setValue and simulated that fixing overlay breaks it (0xFFFFFF00ABCD1234 against 0xAB421234) while a compose fix passes the trigger, so it was converging on the gold. It spent its last 4 calls on git log/show history probes, which the protocol forbids, and hit the 50-call limit without submitting.

On the control, the agent confirmed by simulation around call 29 that 'the bug is in NumberUtils.overlay: shift = (index + at) * width should be index * width + at'. It then spent roughly 20 calls on bash comment notes, git log, @since greps and sibling browsing while assembling 10 names, and hit the 50-call limit without submitting.

defects4j ran here but printed only 'Failing tests: 1'. A Java simulation gave 112.5, leading to 'drift() has reversed subtraction order. Should compute point2-point1'. It called nudge 'correct in isolation' and ranked it 5th. Its caller greps explicitly filtered out test files (grep -v 'test\|Test'), so testDrift could not surface.

pattern: Chunk 2/6 of the adversarial-break-v1 wrong runs: 15 runs, of which 9 answered wrong, 5 ran out of budget and 1 was a provider stall. The gold body was shown and fully read in all 15 runs, so there are no SEARCH_FAILURE or DISCOVERY_WITHOUT_INSPECTION cases. Every miss is a failure of attribution, not of discovery. (1) Chart definer family (DEFINER-01 and COMPOSITE-01; 6 answers: Opus 2/3, Sonnet 5/5/5/5): every answer ranked PlotUtilities.drift first on an unverified 'drift should be p2-p1 / exploded minus unexploded' convention. Each agent first reproduced 112.5 by its own simulation; reversing drift then fixes it, and that settled the choice. In every case, drift-caller greps were limited to source/, and one explicitly excluded tests, so PlotUtilitiesTests.testDrift was never retrieved. Sonnet also put the shallow hops (rim, ring, getArcBounds) above the gold adapter, while Opus put the gold at 2 or 3. The COMPOSITE padding did not stop gold reading: both runs read resolve's delta lines. (2) Lang MASK-01: both answered runs ranked overlay first and compose 4th, in strict depth order. Opus never looked up overlay's second caller (retrieval failure). Sonnet run-007 retrieved setValue and correctly derived that the field must be pre-shifted, yet still blamed overlay (integration failure). Sonnet run-013 reached the right inference but spent its remaining calls on git-history probes and ran out of budget. Haiku found setValue only at its last two calls. (3) LEX-01: Sonnet followed the javadoc/body mismatch in wordOffset even after displaying widen, where wordOffset only feeds a guard. (4) The non-answers are mostly not reasoning failures: Haiku ran out of budget in all three of its runs; in the CONVERSION-LONG control both Haiku and Sonnet had diagnosed overlay correctly but never submitted, spending calls on notes and test-runner hunting. defects4j test failed everywhere except the sonnet46t runner, because the Perl module String::Interpolate is missing, and even there it printed no values. Agents therefore got failure values only by re-simulating the code, which reproduces the symptom but cannot settle ownership. Several Sonnet runs also probed git log/diff, which the protocol forbids.
